businessContact.emailStatus: no canonical submission email; adjacent first-party and conditional programme mailboxes excluded
businessContact.verification: The official Contact page states that music is not considered by email and directs artists to the submission form. The Privacy page publishes hello@freshonthe.net for personal-data requests, not music. The Submit page separately publishes del.owusu@gmail.com for a conditional Exile FM clean-radio-edit route that requires prior Fresh On The Net submission. Both addresses have valid syntax and first-party publication, but neither is stored as the canonical Fresh On The Net submission route. No SMTP, MX, catch-all, mailbox-level or deliverability probing was performed.

formBoundary.manualRecheckReason: The route is schedule- and capacity-gated. Fresh On The Net says the inbox opens Monday morning and closes after 200 tracks or by Wednesday evening. On July 16, 2026 the official page displayed the inbox as closed and indicated a July 20 reopening boundary. A current live-form representation exposed artist name, track name, SoundCloud URL and a terms checkbox but no visible CAPTCHA, login or payment. The live anti-spam and consent state must be rechecked when the inbox opens. Current first-party pages also conflict on whether AI-assisted music may be declared or whether all AI-generated tracks are prohibited, so a human provenance decision is mandatory.
adjacentRoutesExcluded: conditional Exile FM clean-edit mailbox published on the Submit page
direct email or CD delivery to Fresh On The Net or Tom Robinson
individual volunteer and moderator social-media accounts
BBC Introducing uploader as a substitute for the Fresh On The Net form

activityVerification.evidence: Fresh On The Net's official site published Listening Post and Fresh Faves Batch 615 activity in July 2026, including Fresh Faves dated July 13 and Alt Picks dated July 14. The homepage and archive continue to expose current weekly batches, and the submission page publishes a current July 20 reopening boundary.

genreFitEvidence: Fresh On The Net describes itself as a resource and discovery platform for independent recording artists and welcomes any artist with a new track.
The weekly Listening Post and Fresh Faves workflow is editorially broad rather than restricted to a single genre.
Selected MarcsMusic electronic, bass, reggae, world-fusion, pop and alternative tracks may be editorially relevant only if they satisfy the current provenance, SoundCloud and repeat-submission rules.
newPlatforms.manualReviewReason: Fresh On The Net explicitly authorizes one weekly track through its first-party SoundCloud-link form, but the inbox is schedule/capacity gated and was closed on July 16, 2026. A human must wait for the official opening, inspect live anti-spam and consent controls, apply the strictest current AI-provenance rule because first-party pages conflict, verify public worldwide SoundCloud availability and embeddability, confirm the track has not previously been submitted and is not a disallowed remix or alternate version, accept the terms, and submit only one track. Email, CD, privacy-mailbox, individual-volunteer, conditional Exile FM and BBC uploader routes must not be used as substitutes.

deduplication.repositoryEvidence: The complete open pull-request patch and repository code index were searched for Fresh On The Net, freshonthenet.co.uk, freshonthe.net, Fresh Faves, Listening Post and Send Us A Track. No prior music-submission-agent platform, runtime seed or queue record was found.
deduplication.consolidation: The weekly first-party form is stored once as the canonical Fresh On The Net opportunity. The privacy mailbox, conditional Exile FM route, direct email/CD delivery, individual volunteers and BBC Introducing uploader are excluded as parallel or substitute opportunities.

notes: One new free-first Fresh On The Net opportunity was queued as needs_manual_review. No form field, terms checkbox, SoundCloud URL, email, file, login, CAPTCHA or payment was submitted.
